claims.text: A critical outward-diffusion-rate threshold for high-oxygen-affinity elements governs formation and maintenance of a continuous, self-healing oxide scale in MPEAs.
Diffusion above the critical rate produces a coherent, adherent protective oxide scale.
A coherent protective oxide scale inhibits further oxidation.
Maintaining a protective oxide scale preserves the alloy's mechanical or structural integrity.
Diffusion below the critical rate prevents continuous repair of the scale and causes discontinuous or porous oxide formation.
Discontinuous or porous scales cause accelerated oxidation and degradation of material integrity.
Near-equiatomic multi-element alloys can exist as solid solutions.
Slight enrichment or depletion of Cr relative to Mn alters the individual diffusion rates of protective elements.
Oxygen partial pressure and temperature affect time-dependent oxide phase formation in CrMnFeCoNi.
Oxygen-isotope labeling can be used to monitor the relevant elemental diffusion kinetics.
The balance between elemental diffusion flux and oxide-growth kinetics dictates whether a continuous protective scale forms.
Higher Cr diffusion rates promote rapid oxide formation and repair, producing a self-healing scale.
Cr is more likely than Mn to generate a protective oxide in the proposed Cr-Mn-containing MPEA comparison.
Slight Cr enrichment will increase the Cr diffusion rate relative to the baseline alloy.
Cr-enriched alloys will form thicker, more continuous, and more adherent protective oxide scales than the baseline alloy.
Cr-enriched alloys will oxidize more slowly than the baseline alloy.
Cr-depleted alloys will exhibit nonuniform oxide scales and higher oxidation rates than the baseline alloy.
The proposed diffusion-threshold behavior applies over approximately 800–1100 °C and oxygen partial pressures from low controlled levels to 1 atm.
Severely reducing atmospheres or temperatures causing extreme scale spallation may produce behavior outside the proposed mechanism.

Failure of Cr-enriched samples to show improved scale continuity and adherence, lower oxidation kinetics, and better retained mechanical properties would falsify the proposed diffusion-threshold mechanism.
